Then $V(x) = (1 + x)(2 + x)(4 + x)$.Solve ($1 + x)(2 + x)(4 + x) = 9(1)(2)(4)$. $P(x) = x^3 + 7x 2 + 14x - 64 6 F P(x) = x^3 + 7x 2 + 14x - 64 P(2) = (2) 3 + 7(2) 2 + 14(2) - 64 = 8 + 28 + 28 - 64 P(2) = 0$ Let $7x 2 + 14x - 64 = 0 (x - 2)(x^2 + 9x + 32) = 0 x = 2 or x^2 + 9x + 32 = 0$, and try x $= 2$ in the factor theorem. $9x + 32 = 0 = z0 z0$ Thus, x $2$ is a factor of $P(x)$. bodyIssues.body: Let x represent the side length of the square to be cut from each corner.Then $V(x) = x(15$ – $2x)(25$ – $2x)$.Solve $x(15$ – $2x)(25$ – $2x) = 476$. $x = 1 3 .$ Let $P(x) = 4x 3 - 80x 2 + 375x - 476$, and try x $= 4$ in the factor theorem. $P(x) = 4x 3 - 80x 2 + 375x - 476 P(4) = 4(4) 3 - 80(4 2 ) + 375(4) - 476 = 256 - 1280 + 1500 - 476 P(4) = 0$ Thus, x $4$ is a factor of $P(x)$. Divide to find another factor. $4x 3 - 80x 2 + 375x - 476 = 0 (x - 4)(4x 2 - 64x + 119) = 0 x = 4$ Thus, $x = 64 ( - 64) 2 - 4(4)(119) 2(4) = 16 137 2 13.9$ Use the quadratic formula to solve the quadratic equation. [DIAGRAM NEEDED] x $= 13.9$ cm is not possible because of the starting dimensions of the sheet of metal. The side length of the square cut from each corner is either $4$ cm or approximately $2.15$ cm.
